topic: how does the TCP handshake work
narration: Say your laptop talks to a server. First, your laptop sends a SYN. Think knock knock. It says, I want to talk, starting at number forty two. Second, the server replies with SYN ACK. That means, heard you, I'm starting at one hundred, and I expect forty three next. Third, your laptop sends a final ACK. Got it, expect one oh one next. Now both sides proved they can send and receive, and locked their counters.
description: Clean 2D side view, same dark background, laptop left-mid (accent=cyan) and server right-mid (accent2=magenta) larger. Straight fg=white horizontal wire between them at 45% height. Numbered envelope packets travel along wire: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. Above laptop a counter box shows MY SEQ with number 42; above server a counter box shows MY SEQ with number 100 and EXPECT. Counters start muted=grey and turn good=green with lock icon when acknowledged. Single focal packet moves at a time. Kinetic labels SYN, SYN ACK, ACK pop center above wire.

beats.action: Clean side view settles: laptop left glows accent, server right glows accent2, empty wire between, empty counter boxes above each in muted.
Laptop enlarges and glows brighter; label 'SYN' in accent pops above wire at laptop side.
Accent envelope labeled SYN SEQ 42 travels laptop to server along wire.
Counter above laptop flips from muted to show 42 in fg=white; label 'starting at 42' appears.
Server enlarges and glows brighter; label 'SYN ACK' in accent2 pops above wire at server side.
Accent2 envelope labeled SYN SEQ 100 ACK 43 travels server to laptop along wire.
Laptop glows again; small accent3 envelope labeled ACK forms at laptop.
Accent3 envelope labeled ACK 101 travels laptop to server; laptop counter shows EXPECT 101.
Both counter boxes flash good=green with white lock icons; wire turns solid good=green showing locked connection.
